tasks.title: Define and Implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
tasks.description:
Design and implement a role-based access control system to manage user permissions across different areas of the application.

Scope:
1. **Role Definitions:**
   - Identify key user roles (e.g., Admin, Editor, Viewer).
   - Define access rights and restrictions for each role (e.g., edit rights, data visibility).

2. **Backend Implementation:**
   - Add roles and permission logic to the user model.
   - Implement middleware that restricts access to protected routes based on user role.

3. **Frontend Adjustments:**
   - Dynamically hide or show UI components depending on the user's role.
   - Disable buttons/actions if the user lacks permission.

4. **Testing:**
   - Verify that each role can only perform permitted actions.
   - Include test users for each role and validate workflows.

Quality Criteria:
- Roles and permissions clearly documented.
- Unauthorized access attempts are blocked on backend.
- UI updates based on user roles without errors.
- Functionality tested with at least 3 role types.

User Benefits:
- Secure and predictable access aligned with user responsibilities.
- Cleaner UI based on user needs (e.g., viewers won’t see admin features).
- Reduces risk of accidental changes or data exposure.
tasks.comments: This task will lay the foundation for secure and scalable user management. Role design must align with business requirements before implementation begins.

tasks.title: Implement Login Function
tasks.description:
Develop and implement a secure, responsive login function with third-party authentication (OAuth 2.0) and seamless frontend integration.

Scope:
1. **Backend Integration:**
   - Implement OAuth 2.0 login flow using providers Google and GitHub.
   - Use Passport.js middleware for Node.js to handle authentication and token exchange.
   - Configure callback URLs and environment-based client secrets.
   - Implement session management using JSON Web Tokens (JWT).

2. **Frontend Login Page:**
   - Build a responsive login form with Vue.js.
   - Include branded buttons for Google and GitHub login.
   - Add loading indicators, error feedback (e.g., access denied, invalid credentials), and accessibility (ARIA labels).

3. **Session Handling & Security:**
   - Store JWT securely in HttpOnly cookies.
   - Implement logout functionality and session expiration.
   - Enforce HTTPS and CORS policy for token exchange.

4. **Error Handling & Logging:**
   - Display user-friendly error messages (e.g., access denied, timeout).
   - Log login attempts (provider, timestamp, user ID) for audit purposes.

Quality Criteria:
- Users can log in via Google or GitHub and are redirected to dashboard on success.
- Session cookie is secure and persists for the expected duration.
- Login UI is fully responsive and accessible on desktop and mobile.
- Login tested across major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari).
- Unit tests validate login state transitions and token handling.
- Authentication errors handled gracefully with retry options.

User Benefits:
- Fast and secure login without needing to create new credentials.
- Familiar authentication experience through trusted providers.
- Peace of mind through improved security and session control.
- Smooth experience across mobile and desktop devices.
- Transparent feedback when something goes wrong during login.
tasks.comments:
OAuth 2.0 backend integration with Google and GitHub was successfully completed using Passport.js.
Frontend login form created with responsive layout using Tailwind CSS.
JWT session handling partially implemented — currently working on cookie security flags and logout logic.
Initial testing on Chrome and Firefox successful; Safari testing planned.
UI error handling with toast notifications is in progress.

workLogs.description: Implemented OAuth 2.0 integration with Google and GitHub using Passport.js. Set up environment variables and redirect routes for both providers. Tokens are being received and processed correctly.
Designed and implemented the responsive login page using Vue and Tailwind CSS. Added OAuth login buttons and basic error placeholders. Verified compatibility on desktop and mobile devices.
Added JWT-based session handling with HttpOnly cookies and expiration policy. Started implementing logout route and cookie cleanup. Added server-side error logging for failed authentications.

tasks.title: Set Up CI/CD Pipeline for Automated Deployment
tasks.description:
Establish a Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline to automate the build, test, and deployment process from the start of the project.

Scope:
1. **CI Pipeline:**
   - Configure build pipeline using GitHub Actions (or GitLab CI, Azure DevOps depending on infrastructure).
   - Install dependencies, run linter, and execute unit tests on every push to `main` and feature branches.

2. **CD Pipeline:**
   - Deploy to development/staging environment on push to `main`.
   - Add manual approval step for production deployment.
   - Use Docker and environment-based config for portability.

3. **Secrets & Environment Setup:**
   - Store sensitive credentials securely in GitHub Secrets or Azure Key Vault.
   - Set up `.env` support and encrypted config for multiple environments.

4. **Notification & Rollback:**
   - Configure Slack or Teams notifications on build/deploy status.
   - Enable rollback to last successful deployment on failure.

Quality Criteria:
- Build runs automatically on code push with linter + test feedback
- Deployment to staging within 5 minutes of push to `main`
- Secrets and environment configs handled securely
- Teams notified on success/failure events
tasks.comments:
CI/CD was set up using GitHub Actions with Docker-based build steps. A `ci.yml` workflow file was created to lint, build, and test the application automatically on every push. For CD, a second workflow deploys the Docker image to the staging environment using GitHub Secrets for credentials and SSH key-based deployment.

Slack notifications were added to inform the dev team on successful or failed deployments. Environment configuration is handled via `.env.staging` and `.env.production` files, encrypted using Mozilla SOPS and stored securely.

**Benefits:**
- 🧑‍💻 **For Developers/Users**: Immediate feedback on code quality and faster iterations
- 🏢 **For Organization**: Fewer manual steps, more reliable and secure releases, standardization
- 📈 **For Management**: Shorter time-to-market, improved transparency via automatic logs and metrics

Rollback is supported via tagged Docker images and versioned releases.

workLogs.description: Configured GitHub Actions CI workflow with build, lint, and test stages. Added caching for dependencies and parallel job execution.
Created CD pipeline for auto-deployment to staging using Docker and SSH. Verified container health checks post-deploy.
Set up Slack integration for CI/CD status notifications. Wrote internal guide for developers on how to use and trigger the pipeline.
